record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.context_brief: Comparing resolvent and subgraph interlacing counts
record.original_question: For a graph G with adjacency matrix A and spectral radius ρ, the resolvent centrality of vertex i is RC(i, α) = [(I − αA)^{-1}]_{ii} for 0 < α < 1/ρ. For a fixed pair of vertices, compare the numbers of interlacing values for resolvent centrality and exponential subgraph centrality. Is it always true that the number of α for which RC(i, α) = RC(j, α) is less than or equal to the number of β for which [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}? Prove or disprove this statement.

evidence.quote: The resolvent centrality [15] (also called resolvent subgraph centrality) with parameter α is defined as follows: RC(i, α) = [( I − αA)− 1]ii.

Problem 4. For a given pair of vertices of a graph G, prove or disprove the following statement: the number of interlacing values relative to resolvent centrality is always less than or equal to the number of interlacing values relative to subgraph centrality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$ and spectral radius $\rho = \rho(A)$. For a vertex $i$ of $G$ and a real parameter $\alpha$ with $0 < \alpha < 1/\rho$, define the resolvent (subgraph) centrality of $i$ by
$$RC(i,\alpha) = \bigl[(I - \alpha A)^{-1}\bigr]_{ii},$$
and for a real parameter $\beta > 0$ define the exponential subgraph centrality of $i$ by
$$SC(i,\beta) = \bigl[e^{\beta A}\bigr]_{ii}.$$
For a fixed pair of distinct vertices $i,j$ of $G$, call a value of the parameter an "interlacing value" for the respective centrality if the centralities of $i$ and $j$ coincide there: i.e. an $\alpha \in (0, 1/\rho)$ with $RC(i,\alpha) = RC(j,\alpha)$, or a $\beta > 0$ with $SC(i,\beta) = SC(j,\beta)$.

Let $N_{RC}(i,j)$ denote the number of interlacing values of $\alpha \in (0, 1/\rho)$ for the resolvent centrality and let $N_{SC}(i,j)$ denote the number of interlacing values of $\beta > 0$ for the exponential subgraph centrality.

Prove or disprove: for every graph $G$ and every pair of distinct vertices $i,j$,
$$N_{RC}(i,j) \;\le\; N_{SC}(i,j).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in the work introducing it, and a search does not reveal any subsequent publication resolving the inequality between the counts of interlacing values for resolvent centrality and exponential subgraph centrality for general graphs. No proof or counterexample has been located.

status_evidence.claim: The comparison is posed as an open problem with no known resolution.

status_evidence.title: Matching exponential-based and resolvent-based centrality measures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the relationship between resolvent-based and exponential-based centrality measures, matching parameters between them, but does not establish the interlacing-count inequality.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature studies matching of the two families but does not settle the interlacing-count comparison.
